title: Demonstrating sheet music at Jones Music Store
summary: Soon after arriving in Chicago in 1918 she got a job playing songs at a State Street music store, learning the stock and drawing crowds.

story.theme_name: First paying gigs: getting started as a young professional
story.community_name: First paid gigs: pay, bands and young beginnings

blocks.x: Oh, it was, um, well, we moved here the last part of, uh, 1918. And, um, I was to go back to school the following, uh, September. In the meantime, I went down State Street one day, and I passed this music store, with all this music in the window, so I went in and asked the lady for a song, that I had heard, but I didn't know the name of it, so I hummed it over, and, uh, they had a man there, playing, demonstrating music, and he said, oh, I know what it is, so, he played it, oh, for me, but he didn't play it so well, so I said, let me play it. And, uh, he said, okay, so I played it, and he said, oh, you can play, and he said, you want a job demonstrating music? I said, oh, I don't know, I said, I just want to buy this piece of music, so he said, well, come back at three o'clock this afternoon, and see the boss, so I went back to three o'clock that afternoon, and, uh, when I walked in, the lady said, miss, his name was Frank, so he said, Mrs. Jones was the lady, his name who owned the stores, was Jones Music's store, so she said, oh, Frank, this is nothing but a child. He said, but I don't care, she can play, he said, play something for us, so I, so he put a couple of pieces of sheet music on the piano, and I played them for, and she said, oh, well, all right, she said, honey, if you want to work, I'll give you three dollars a week, well, I didn't worry about the three dollars a week, all I wanted to do was to learn all the music, without having to buy it, so I went home, told my mother, I had a job playing this music store, for three dollars a week, so she said, no, indeed, you have not, you will not work for three dollars a week, I said, oh, I just want to learn all the music, I said, they got a, oh, the counters and counters, full of music, and I can learn it, you don't have to buy it, and she said, well, all right, if that's all you want to do, so I started right away to memorize all the pieces, because I didn't know how long I'd be there, well, after the, two or three days, everybody that came in the store, they would stand around the piano, and, and listen to me play, I had learned all the music, and I'd be getting to add some extra things to it, and then I was playing my little classical pieces, you know, so I became the talk of the neighborhood, little girl down the music store playing, and about the third week, oh, yes, the second week I was there, she raised me five dollars, she gave me eight dollars, because the people had began to come in and listen, and, so, well, I'm talking pretty fast, huh, too fast?
